questions.text: Which computer device, named after a small rodent, moves the on-screen pointer?
questions.explanation: The computer mouse was demonstrated by Douglas Engelbart in 1968.

questions.text: In the abbreviation CPU, what does the 'C' stand for?
questions.explanation: CPU stands for central processing unit.

questions.text: Which company created the Windows operating system?
Who co-founded Apple with Steve Jobs in 1976?
questions.explanation: Wozniak designed the Apple I and Apple II computers.

questions.text: Which company launched the iPhone in 2007?
questions.explanation: Steve Jobs unveiled the first iPhone in January 2007.

questions.text: Who is credited with inventing the World Wide Web in 1989?
questions.explanation: Berners-Lee proposed the Web while working at CERN.

questions.text: Which programmable electronic computer, completed in 1945, was built at the University of Pennsylvania?
questions.explanation: ENIAC was an early general-purpose electronic digital computer.

questions.text: Which programming language was released by Sun Microsystems in 1995?
questions.explanation: Java was designed by James Gosling's team at Sun.

questions.text: Which graphical web browser, released in 1993 by the NCSA, helped popularise the Web?
questions.explanation: Mosaic was developed at the University of Illinois NCSA.

questions.text: The C64, a hugely popular 1980s home computer, was made by which firm?
Which British mathematician described a 'universal machine' in a 1936 paper?
questions.explanation: Turing's paper laid foundations for theoretical computer science.

questions.text: Which Victorian inventor designed the Analytical Engine, which Ada Lovelace wrote about?
questions.explanation: Babbage designed the Analytical Engine in the 1830s, though it was never completed.

questions.text: Which Intel chip, released in 1971, is considered the first commercial microprocessor?
questions.explanation: The 4004 was a 4-bit CPU originally designed for a calculator.

questions.text: Which programming language did Dennis Ritchie develop at Bell Labs in the early 1970s?
questions.explanation: C was created alongside the Unix operating system.

questions.text: Which US Navy officer led the team that developed FLOW-MATIC and championed machine-independent languages?

spares.text: Which key do you press to start a new line when typing?
spares.explanation: The Enter or Return key inserts a line break.

spares.text: Which social network was founded in 2004 by Mark Zuckerberg and fellow Harvard students?
spares.explanation: It began as a Harvard-only site before opening more widely.

spares.text: What was the name of the IBM computer that beat chess champion Garry Kasparov in 1997?
spares.explanation: Deep Blue won a six-game match 3.5 to 2.5.

spares.text: ARPANET, a forerunner of the Internet, was funded by which organisation?
spares.explanation: ARPA was a Defense Department research agency.
